title: Phase matching selects background dips in shear tests on 126 TESS CPV visits
abstract: We test whether phase proximity identifies an added shearing clump in complex periodic variable light curves. We use published 15-harmonic models and noise thresholds for 126 TESS visits in 60 stars. We run 5,040 model-space trials with two phases, two initial depths, four radial spreads, real or flat backgrounds, and zero-signal controls. A uniform random phase has an exact mean chance of 18.3% of matching an existing long track (95% star-bootstrap interval 14.6-22.3%). At a full fractional radial spread of 0.01, phase matching gives 52 and 92 recoveries out of 252 trials at each depth. A known-signal curvature check reduces these counts to 3 and 36. All 17 long, strong matches at this spread give width-based radial limits below half the known input; their median limits are about twenty times too small. None passes the curvature check. Flat-background controls give no long, strong matches at spreads of 0.002 or 0.01. Thus phase matching can select a narrow background dip after the added clump spreads. This limits the use of injection recovery to support material-width bounds. It does not show that free gas explains long CPV dips, or invalidate the geometric bound for an isolated identified profile. These are model-space tests, not a repeat of cadence-level processing or a measurement of material life. Code, trial results, aggregate intervals, input hashes and separate-scratch reproduction steps are included.

display.caption: Model-space injection recovery, known-signal curvature checks, and large errors in width-based radial limits. Each rate uses all 252 trials in that group. Flat backgrounds separate signal loss from confusion with real CPV patterns.

citations.reason: Uses its published TESS window models, visit and track tables, detector and linker. Tests its phase-only shear recovery rule. Challenges the sufficiency of that rule for identifying the added clump, not the observed existence of slow dip drift.
Prior harmonic-phase test of symmetric smearing; distinct from source identity during injection recovery.
Parent selection of on-target CPV hosts, inherited through the window study. No Gaia record table is used.
